note: Source of truth for the Structures page (structures.html) — canonical maps of the psyche, plus this site's own model. Each structure renders as a stack of labelled bands: form 'strata' = full-width bands; form 'pyramid' = bands that widen toward the base. 'layers' are written top-to-bottom as they should appear. Editorial prose — refine freely. Literal Unicode only, no HTML entities.

structures.name: The Foundations of a Self
structures.intro: Not how the self was formed — that is the clinic's map — but what a strong one is built on, and the order of the work. The Psyche's first series climbs this ladder from the ground up.

layers.label: Purpose
layers.note: A why you can carry almost any how toward. Without it, no technique holds.

layers.label: Discipline
layers.note: Choosing what you want most over what you want now. Motivation is a liar; acting anyway is freedom.

layers.label: Fear
layers.note: Almost every flaw is fear in costume. Love, openness and presence are what remain when it leaves.

layers.label: Agency
layers.note: Author, not victim. You do not choose the weather; you author the response — always. The keystone.

layers.label: Worth
layers.note: Built, not handed out; non-contingent, owned outright. The ground everything else stands on.

structures.caveat: A curriculum, not a diagnosis. The order is deliberate — nothing above holds until Worth and Agency are under it.

structures.name: Freud's Structural Model
structures.intro: The mind read as three forces in constant negotiation, most of it below the waterline of awareness. A century old and much revised — but still the vocabulary everyone borrows.

layers.label: Superego
layers.note: The internalised rules and ideals — conscience, and the image of who you ought to be.

layers.label: Ego
layers.note: The negotiator and reality-tester, brokering between drive, conscience, and the world as it is.

layers.label: Id
layers.note: The reservoir of drive and appetite — wants, now, without limit or logic.

structures.caveat: A historical map, not a brain diagram. Treat it as a useful metaphor for inner conflict, not a literal anatomy.

structures.name: Jung's Model of the Psyche
structures.kicker: From the mask to the Self
structures.intro: Consciousness as a small lit circle inside a vast inherited dark. Individuation is the long work of moving from the outermost mask down toward the Self at the centre.

layers.label: Persona
layers.note: The mask worn for the world — useful, until you mistake it for the whole of you.

layers.label: Ego
layers.note: The centre of consciousness; the 'I' that knows itself.

layers.label: Personal Unconscious
layers.note: Forgotten and repressed material, gathered into charged complexes.

layers.label: The Shadow
layers.note: What the ego disowns — refused, and therefore where much of the power is kept.

layers.label: Anima / Animus
layers.note: The contrasexual inner figure; the bridge from the ego down into the depths.

layers.label: Collective Unconscious
layers.note: Inherited patterns shared across all people — the archetypes.

layers.label: The Self
layers.note: The centre and totality of the whole psyche; what individuation moves toward.

structures.caveat: Read outer-to-inner: this is a depth gradient, not a ranking — the Self is the core, not the top.

structures.name: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
structures.intro: A ladder of human needs, each rung said to press hardest once the ones below it are reasonably met — from staying alive at the base to becoming fully yourself at the top.

layers.label: Self-Actualisation
layers.note: Becoming what you are capable of — growth, meaning, the fullest use of the self.

layers.label: Esteem
layers.note: Competence, respect, and standing — both earned and given.

layers.label: Love & Belonging
layers.note: Intimacy, friendship, being part of something.

layers.label: Safety
layers.note: Security of body, resources, and a predictable world.

layers.label: Physiological
layers.note: Air, water, food, warmth, rest — the body kept alive.

structures.caveat: The strict 'lower needs first' ordering is contested — people reach for meaning under hardship all the time. Hold it as a rough map, not a law.
